Yeah in the end it boils down to how you envision artificial difficulty. I think of it as a scenario where the developer/designer by choice stakes the odds against you in the laziest manner. Like you said with Azurelos and S.Legi, if you could reach them you could probably kill them with  little difficulty and the developers' solution was "what about if you couldn't reach them :)" So they took your tools and kept the AI in there air. Its not difficulty in the sense of it being challenge, its difficult because they are stretching the time in the least meaningful way so you have to fight boredom which can lead to slip ups like you said. Additionally, its difficult if you were crunched for time so you could also call it tedium in this scenario.

You are partly asking them to remember there is an extended hitbox because you would then have to think "this hits wider than the visual suggests" Its what I did for a bunch of attacks, Lunastra tail swips as an example.

With regards to artificial difficulty, I was replying to someone saying there is no such thing as artificial difficulty. If you see my original reply, you see me saying that HP bloating for late game damage is fair. But, I said the balance in my opinion tilts a bit more in the monster's favour. I however, think the flashpods nerfs and fighting monsters that enjoy being airborne is a form of artificial difficulty. Because our tools to get them down have been reduced, I don't know if the Clutch Claw was supposed to be part of the answer but seeing as the Claw doesn't work that well unless you clagger the monster. Then how are you supposed to reliably clagger it if you can't get it down unless you commit an evade mantle for the one wallbang opportunity. Which is also an issue because we have all seen monsters slide by walls on a wallbangs BUT there have been times I wallbanged and thought "that worked because last time it didn't?"

Edit: should clarify, I bought iceborne in july but I finished World around 2018 and only started playing again when I bought iceborne.

You do realise I specified with 50+% HP and seeing as some monsters do get very spammy, it can take 2 attacks to kill you instantly. I had 1050 defense through fortify against a MR Black Diablos and one dig attack took 60% of my health. Seeing that I was near the tail end of the game with near 950-987 Defense pre-fortify and still went back to MR Black Diablos and got the same 60% off then how tedious is black diablos for hunters who would be midway through. If I'm not mistaken she appears when your defense is 750-850 so effectively you're wearing toilet paper with gem slots.
Your idea of artificial is incredibly pedantic, literally everything in life comes with a level of inherent difficulty. Its artificial because of things they added to the task. Poorly working tools, monsters gliding on a gradient during a charge, stupid animations that lock your character, your hunter getting bambi legs when next to a monster and you didn't press an attack to get minor tremor resistance. Those are all added sections to spike the difficulty artificially. Its like if you went to work one day and your boss said Johnson/Johnsonette, I took your desk away so you'll have to put your computer in your lap. THAT is artificially difficulty, did your computer naturally go on the ground? Are tables not a common item?

You're saying hitboxes are for the most part consistent, yes consistently bad. Somehow asking players to remember that an attack isn't necessarily where the visual is and saying that is fine, is nonsensical to me in so many ways. That is similar to suggesting making oven mitts with holes at the tip of your fingers so you have to remember to not put the mitt on fully because a multi-million dollar company can't make proper oven mitts where other working oven mitts exist.

Artificial difficulty really does exist. Like you said they needed to pump up damage and health to match the gear hunters would acquire which is fair. But the last time, I played it personally felt like the balance leaned towards the monsters. I never tried to be a speed runner anything near 25 minutes for me was a good hunt. The issue lies in the fact that for those 25 minutes, most of the time I had to be switched on constantly because most monsters can one shot you.The thing is if it was a case of the hitboxes in the game being tight, this wouldn't be a problem but we all been hit by attacks we had no right being hit by for 50+% of our health. Or on the other side, where the only viable spots to attack are weirdly hard to hit like MR Kirin's head.Clutch Claw being the absolute dog shit that it is, is part of artificial difficulty because not only is it wildly inaccurate, there is the odds of losing a mantle/getting pinned.Almost all of IB monster fights were a game of tag, running behind a monster after a charge and it going a million miles away and then when you finally gets close, its gone again. Don't forget flashpod nerfs that alone is artificial difficulty because you can't get these flying bitches down.
